findings.title: Within-season centering (base.zwithin / I0010 demean) makes the POOLED interaction dR2 depend on full-season means
construction_lines: w["O"] = zwithin(w, "own_pre");  w["D"] = zwithin(w, "def_pre");  w["OD"] = w["O"] * w["D"]
g = w if seas == "POOLED" else w[w["season"] == seas]
findings.classification: RETROSPECTIVE_SAME_SEASON (centering) and RETROSPECTIVE_CROSS_SEASON (the pooled residualization and sd)
findings.why: The centering constant is the FULL-SEASON mean of the predictor -- a mid-season forecaster does not know it. For MAIN effects a constant shift is absorbed by the intercept and is R2-neutral, so this would be harmless; but the headline metric is dR2_OxM, a PRODUCT of centered terms. Subtracting a SEASON-SPECIFIC mean inside a POOLED regression whose base model has no season dummies is equivalent to adding season-dummy x O terms that are not in the base model, so it genuinely changes the pooled column space and hence the pooled R2. Mres is additionally residualized on D and OD over the whole pooled 2021-2024 sample, and rescaled by a pooled sd.
dependent_claims: E0_I0012_layer3_noncollinear headline pooled dR2_M / dR2_OxM (make_findings.py:342 'pooled dR2 0.000455', :360 'pooled dR2_OxM 0.001071')
E0_I0010_positional_matchup analyze.py:166 (its own demean(), keys=(season,pos_group)), which forms w["OA"] = w["O"] * w["A"]
findings.clean_variant_note: The per-season rows in the same tables are much less affected (within one season the centering constant is a within-sample constant), so a per-season reading is the closer-to-honest one already published.
findings.caveat: This is an AGGREGATE-level preprocessing leak, not row-level hindsight. It is categorically milder than a leave-one-out and I have NOT quantified its magnitude -- doing so requires rebuilding each screen's frame, which is outside a read-only audit. Reported because the screens' own FINDINGS describe these arms as 'fully pregame-observable', which is not literally true.
